3. The defendant contested the suit by filing written statement contending inter-alia that although the suit property was settled with the plaintiff through the settlement case No XII B-9/7576 and a deed of settlement being No. 1566 dated 30.1.1978 was executed and registered in his favour, but the same has been done inadvertently without following the rules in this respect and therefore the settlement is liable to be cancelled. Further the suit property is required for the development of Gopalgonj town and as such the government requires the property for which the settlement was cancelled and the possession has been taken over by the government. 

 11. The learned Advocate Mr. Md. Mesbahul Islam, appearing on behalf of the petitioner while taken this Court through materials on record streneously argued that the finding of the appellate Court is erroneous in as much as the settlement granted in favour of the plaintiff was under the Provisions of Government Estate manual under which a deed of settlement was executed registered in favour of the plaintiff and as such the cancellation of such settlement by administrative order being illegal ought to be considered as threatening of cancellation of the said settlement and as such spit for permanent injunction is the only method to restrain the government from doing an illegal act and as the plaintiff title to the settled land is still in existence, no suit for declaration is needed to be filed by the plaintiff and the reasoning of the appellate court, not being lawful, caused failure of justice for which the same is required to be interfered with by this Court. 

 12. The learned Assistant Attorney General Mr. Gopal Chandra Saha, appeared on behalf of the state and opposed the rule and categorically submits that there was no threatening on behalf of the government to dispossess the plaintiff from the suit property and since the plaintiff filed the suit for permanent injunction the suit was not maintainable at all. 

 15. It appears that admittedly the settlement of suit property by way of lease was made in favour of the plaintiff through the Settlement Case No. XII B-9/7576, dated 30.1.1978 and the then S. D. 0. (Sub Divisional Officer) Gopalgonj executed a deed of settlement in favour of the plaintiff which was duly registered, being No. 1566, dated 30.1.1978. Such registration of lease deed appears to have been made under the provision of section 81B of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act 1951(in short SAT Act 1951) which runs as follows; 

 Section SIB "Registration of lease deed-Notwithstanding anything contained in section 81 and 81A or any other law for the time being in force, no agricultural or non-agricultural tenancy shall in law be created or deemed to have been created, even after acceptance of salami and / or rent from the lessee, till a deed of lease has been executed in favour of the lessee by any authority competent to grant lease of khas land or any other gazatted officer duly authorized in this behalf and the said lease has been duly registered under the provision of clause (d) of sub-section (1) of section 17 of the Registration Act, 1908". 

 (1) Except as otherwise provided in this part, the rights and liabilities of a holder of non-agricultural land, who has become a tenant under the Government in respect of such land by virtue of the acquisition of the superior right in such land under the provisions of this Act, shall, where the provisions of the East Bengal Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act, 1949, applied to such land, at the time of such acquisition, be regulated by provisions of that Act. 

 Provision that, notwithstanding anything contained in this Act or in any other law for the time being in force or in any contract, no non-agricultural tenant shall sub-let the whole or any part of his tenancy on any terms and conditions whatsoever and, if any tenancy or any part of a tenancy is sub-let in contravention of this provision, the interest of the non-agricultural tenant in the tenancy or in that part of the tenancy, as the case may, shall be extinguished, and the tenancy or the part of the tenancy or the part of the tenancy shall vest in the government from the date of such sub-letting five from all encumbrances.
